summary: Device-posture conditional access blocks JIT access grant to Support Runbook Portal after approval
description: Issue summary: After approvers click 'Grant' on a JIT access request for the internal Support Runbook Portal, the request shows Approved but the requesting user is unable to access the portal and receives a 403 with an Okta error referencing device posture. Impact: Two on-call engineers were blocked from performing emergency runbook steps during a paging event; manual SRE escalation required. Environment: Production, us-west region, Runbook Portal (internal), Okta org with recently enabled device-posture Conditional Access policy. This ticket tracks diagnosis and a safe mitigation path.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a JIT access request for 'runbook-portal:edit' via the Support Portal approver flow.
2) Approver authenticates in Okta, reviews request, and clicks 'Grant'. Okta logs show approval completed.
3) Requesting user attempts to open https://runbooks.internal.redwood.com and is redirected to Okta then receives 403 with message 'Access denied: device posture not compliant'.
4) Repeating flow with a user who has device enrolled works as expected; approval grants immediate access.
logs: 2026-03-12T02:14:03Z - Approval event: okta.event: grant_approved, request_id=JIT-9876, approver=j.kim
2026-03-12T02:15:12Z - Runbook portal returned 403 with header X-Auth-Reason: device_enrollment_required
Okta system log snippet: 'Device not enrolled; conditional access policy "Enforce managed device" blocked session.'
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: JIT grant flow issues with token exchange step — approval completes but the session token lacks device claim required by Conditional Access.
Checked Okta system logs: approval event is recorded, but subsequent token exchange from support-portal to runbook-portal includes scope but omits device_posture claim for non-enrolled devices.

Reproduced locally with test user: when device is not enrolled, Okta prompts for device verification and then denies access despite approval; suggests policy evaluation happens after approval and blocks the session creation.

Observed difference: Managed/enrolled endpoints receive a different OIDC /userinfo response including 'device.enrolled: true', which is used by runbook-portal's authz layer. Non-enrolled flows do not get that claim and are rejected.
temporary_workaround: SRE can generate a short-lived bypass token via the support admin service (manual step documented in Confluence) and attach it to the user's session to allow runbook access during incident response. This is in place for affected requests until policy changes are deployed.
proposed_fix: Coordinate with Identity team to: 1) Update the JIT grant token exchange to include a device_posture evaluation step and return a controlled bypass flag for approved requests issued to non-managed devices, OR 2) Adjust Conditional Access rule to allow JIT-approved sessions through a specific Okta client_id (support-admin) for the Runbook Portal. Prefer solution 1 for least privilege.
rollout_plan: 1) Identity to implement token-exchange change in staging and run a canary with a subset of oncall users. 2) Add observability to log device_posture evaluation events and approval correlation IDs. 3) Deploy to production behind a feature flag for two weeks, monitor access failure rate and incident page time-to-resolution.
follow_up_items: Add clearer UX message in the Runbook Portal when device posture blocks access (linking to enrollment docs).
Create a short runbook for on-call SREs describing the manual bypass token procedure and how to request it from Identity team.
Audit other internal apps using JIT to ensure they don't assume device enrollment claims are present after approval.
resolution: Investigations show the Conditional Access policy evaluates device posture post-approval and the JIT token exchange did not include a special claim to let approved non-enrolled devices in. Identity has scoped a token-exchange change and a safe config tweak for the Okta policy. Temporary bypass procedure used successfully in two incidents. Pending code rollout and policy update.
